system.name: Mugi
system.one_liner: a value-level-parallelism (VLP) accelerator that replaces multipliers with temporal spike-coded comparators and shared accumulators to compute LLM GEMMs and nonlinear operations efficiently

content.subject: how a temporal-coded spike selects an accumulator's value to compute i×w without a real multiplier, then scales to arrays

elements.name: i
elements.role: the input value being encoded as a spike time; e.g. i=3 in the running example

elements.name: c
elements.role: a counting-up cycle counter compared against i every cycle
the temporal converter's equivalence comparator; fires a spike only when c equals i

elements.name: TC
elements.role: Temporal Converter: packages the counter and comparator, emitting one spike at cycle i

elements.name: w
elements.role: the weight value accumulated once per cycle; e.g. w=1

elements.name: ACC
elements.role: accumulator that adds w every cycle, producing a running sum (0,1,2,... at cycles 0,1,2,...)

elements.name: Val
elements.role: the accumulator's output value at a given cycle, equal to (cycle number) x w

elements.name: Sub
elements.role: the temporal-subscription signal (the TC's spike) that captures ACC's value at cycle i, yielding the product iw

elements.name: i[0], i[1], i[k]
elements.role: a batch/vector of input values, each with its own TC, sharing one ACC (value reuse) to compute every element's product in parallel

elements.name: Weights
elements.role: multiple weight columns, each with its own ACC, broadcast to every activation row to form a 2D outer-product array

elements.name: Batched activations
elements.role: multiple activation rows (each its own TC), broadcasting their spikes across every weight column's ACC

relations.what: input i is compared against the counter every cycle
the counter increments each cycle and is compared against i
the equivalence comparator's logic is packaged as the Temporal Converter block
w is added into the accumulator every cycle, building a running sum over time
TC emits a single spike at cycle i
the spike selects (subscribes to) ACC's current value at that cycle, capturing iw
every vector element's own TC subscribes to the same shared ACC output, each at its own cycle (value reuse)
each activation row's spikes broadcast across every weight column's ACC to fill the outer-product array

panels.label: (a) temporal coding
panels.differs: introduces the Temporal Converter: an equivalence comparator fires a red spike only at the cycle where counter c equals input i (shown at c=0, c=1, c=3)

panels.label: (b) target product
panels.differs: states the arithmetic goal directly: i=3 times w=1 equals 3, via ordinary multiplication, as the value the circuit must reproduce

panels.label: (c) accumulation
panels.differs: replaces multiplication with repeated accumulation: feeding w into an ACC every cycle produces the sequence 0..5, matching i·w at cycle i

panels.label: (d) temporal subscription
panels.differs: combines (a) and (c): the TC's spike for i=3 selects ACC's value at cycle 3, capturing Val=iw=3 into a register (Sub)

panels.label: (e) value reuse
panels.differs: shares one ACC across a vector of inputs i[0..k]; each element's own TC subscribes to the same accumulator trace at its own cycle, computing all products in parallel

panels.label: (f) outer product array
panels.differs: arranges multiple weight columns (each its own ACC) against multiple batched-activation rows (each its own TC), broadcasting spikes to fill a 2D array of products

values.what: the running example's concrete input/weight/counter values (i=3, w=1, c=0/1/3), the accumulator's 0-5 sequence, and the resulting product iw=3, plus a second example value i[1]=1
values.linked_by: colour: red marks every occurrence of the value 3 (counter match, spike, captured register); blue marks the second example value 1
values.result_cells: the captured product is shown as a numeral inside a yellow hexagon/register at the end of each subscription lane

content.key_idea: VLP replaces a multiplier with a shared accumulator plus per-input temporal comparators: each input's spike, timed to its own value, subscribes to the accumulator's sum at the right cycle to read off its product, scaling to a full outer-product array.
content.reading_order: Read (a) to (f) left to right, top to bottom: comparator basics, the target product, accumulation, their combination via subscription, then vector and 2D-array replication.

summary: Figure 2 builds up Value Level Parallelism (VLP) through six lettered panels using one running example, i=3 and w=1. (a) shows a Temporal Converter: a counter c compared against i fires a red spike only when c equals i (cycle 3). (b) states the arithmetic target, i times w equals 3. (c) shows an accumulator (ACC) fed w every cycle instead, producing a running sum. (d) combines them: the TC's spike at cycle 3 subscribes to (selects) the ACC's value at that exact cycle, capturing the product Val=iw without ever using a multiplier. (e) shares one ACC across a vector of inputs, each with its own TC and its own spike time, computing every element's product in parallel (value reuse). (f) replicates this across multiple weight columns and batched-activation rows to compute a full outer-product array.
summary_zh: 图2用i=3、w=1逐步构建VLP：(a)c等于i时TC发脉冲；(b)目标积为3；(c)累加器每周期加w得序列；(d)脉冲在第3周期订阅累加值得iw=3；(e)多输入共享累加器并行订阅(值复用)；(f)推广为多列权重与多行激活的外积阵列。
